attempts.summary: Implemented the cross-LAN firewall requirement with an Ansible playbook (cross-lan-firewall.yml + inventory.ini, staged on node4/control_node at /root/ansible-cross-lan-firewall/). It statically addresses node2's lan-a NIC (10.50.10.11/24) and node3's lan-b NIC (10.50.20.12/24) with a specific route to the peer subnet via node1, opens node3's local firewalld only for tcp/5432 from the lan-a CIDR, and configures VyOS (node1) with eth1=10.50.10.254/24, eth2=10.50.20.254/24 and a forward-filter firewall (accept established/related, accept tcp/5432 from eth1->eth2, default-action drop). Verified node2->node3:5432 succeeds while ICMP, other ports, and the reverse direction are all blocked. The tricky part: VyOS's non-interactive config-session setup (cli-shell-api setupSession) silently fails when invoked directly as the 'vyos' user over SSH; the fix was to escalate via the vyos user's passwordless sudo (become: true/sudo) so the VyOS config script runs as root, which reliably creates the config session. All 4 managed nodes were then restarted one at a time, each showing a changed boot_id and full recovery of networking/firewall/tooling state, and the playbook was re-run successfully from node4 after its own reboot to prove Ansible-driven recovery.
